nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life below water|Climate adaptation|Climate change mitigation_qna_000
nodes.question: How are climate change pressures impacting governance levels in terms of policy alignment?
nodes.answer: Climate change pressures are raising CO2 reduction to the highest priority level, alongside 'congestion reduction', at all levels of governance, leading to better alignment of policy aims across different governance levels.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life below water|Climate adaptation|Climate change mitigation_qna_001
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: How does adaptation differ from mitigation when addressing pollution damage?
nodes.answer: Adaptation measures are aimed at reducing the adverse effects of accumulated pollution, while mitigation focuses on curtailing pollution emissions.
nodes.paragraph: Most countries facing a transboundary pollution problem implement one of two political strategies: mitigation and adaptation. Mitigation policies aimed at reducing carbon emissions instead adaptation measures meant to reduce pollution damage, considering the dramatic effects of the accumulation and increase in the concen- tration of pollutant which persists in the atmosphere for decades. While mitigation consists of any means aimed at curtailing the pollution emission of countries, adap- tation is increasingly considered a policy response to climate change alongside the Stability of International Environmental Agreements: Effects mitigation of greenhouse gas emissions, its measures consist of a set of actions that prevent or decrease the adverse effects of accumulated pollution. The literature look - ing at IEAs combining mitigation and adaptation measures is quite recent. Benchek - roun et al. (2017), Borrero and Rubio (2022), Breton and Sbragia (2019), Lazkano et al. (2016), Masoudi and Zaccour (2017), Rohrer and Rubio (2024) and Masoudi and Zaccour (2018) focus on the strategic role of mitigation and adaptation in the IEAs as a tool to combat climate change.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life below water|Climate adaptation|Climate change mitigation_qna_002
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What is the distinction between mitigation and adaptation in the context of climate agreements according to the cited literature?
nodes.answer: Mitigation is considered a public good, while adaptation is viewed as a private good affecting only the host country's welfare, although some studies suggest it may have public good characteristics as well.
nodes.paragraph: While mitigation activity is always consid- ered as a public, international good, about adaptation, different scenarios have been proposed. In Lazkano et al. (2016), Rohrer and Rubio (2024) and Benchekroun et al. (2017) adaptation is a private good that only affects the welfare of the host coun- try instead (Masoudi & Zaccour 2017) and Masoudi and Zaccour (2018) assume that adaptation has a public good flavor. In Bayramoglu et al. (2018) it is studied the strategic interaction between mitigation (public good) and adaptation (private good) in a climate agreement. The view that adaptation is a private good is certainly correct when the focus is on the use of a specific adaptation technology. However, new knowledge about adaptation requires investments in research and development (R&D), which can be shared by different entities, with the resulting new technolo- gies benefiting all parties. All paper cited are modelled as a multi-stage game where players select their level of emissions and their level of adaptation in different stages and results indicate that the simultaneous deciding of adaptation and mitigation levels may have a positive effect on the stability of IEAs.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life below water|Climate adaptation|Climate change mitigation_qna_003
nodes.question: What is the focus of the Contribution of Working Group III to the Sixth Assessment Report of the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change?
nodes.answer: The focus of the Contribution of Working Group III is on the mitigation of climate change.

nodes.question: What are some fundamental factors contributing to the generation of greenhouse gases?
nodes.answer: The identification of fundamental factors contributing to the generation of greenhouse gases is essential for addressing climate change (Rain, 2023f).

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Life below water|Climate adaptation|Climate change mitigation_qna_005
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What is the main inducing factor of climate change mentioned in the paragraph?
nodes.answer: The main inducing factor of climate change mentioned is carbon emissions.
nodes.paragraph: However, the main inducing factor of climate change is carbon emissions, which has been used as a signi cant reference point for the evaluation of future climate change in the prediction models (Tierney et al., 2020 ). In this connection, it can be perceived that reducing carbon emissions is the key to mitigating climate change and enactments of a variety of environmental regulation mechanisms, such as mandatory, voluntary, and market-oriented systems have been observed to reduce emissions (Chen et al., 2021 ). As a market-oriented policy instrument in particular, carbon emissions trading has been recognized to be an effective mechanism to achieve low-cost emissions reduction (Bauer et al., 2020 ; Cui et al., 2014 ; Daskalakis, 2013 ; Zhang & Wei, 2010 ). In the recent decades, China has been facing serious environmental problems. It is pre- dicted that carbon intensity in the middle region will reach the highest in 2023 (Ma et al., 2020 ). The introduction of the Emissions Trading System (ETS) to tackle climate change has therefore been put forward on the policy agenda.
